harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured and verified inventory-worker on node1. It runs as locked, unprivileged inventorysvc inside a root-owned chroot, with /var/lib/inventory as its sole writable application directory. The enabled service recovered after a full node reboot with SELinux enforcing and the original OS/kernel unchanged.
actions_performed: Created the inventorysvc system account with nologin shell and locked password.
Created /srv/inventory-chroot with root-owned executable and directory structure.
Installed and enabled a hardened systemd inventory-worker service.
Bound /usr read-only and /var/lib/inventory read-write into the chroot.
Verified the live worker has UID/GID 992, zero active capabilities, NoNewPrivileges, and a chrooted process root.
Proved writes succeed in /var/lib/inventory but fail in /opt, /usr, and the /var/lib parent.
Restarted node1 safely and verified changed boot identity, service recovery, data health, and continuing heartbeat updates.

evidence.requirement: Preserve installed OS release, kernel, and security controls
evidence.summary: Before and after evidence shows RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0, and SELinux Enforcing.

evidence.requirement: Run inventory-worker as dedicated unprivileged inventorysvc account
evidence.summary: The service is enabled and active with User/Group inventorysvc; the account is locked, and the live process has UID/GID 992 with zero permitted, effective, or ambient capabilities.

evidence.requirement: Confine filesystem view to a root-owned chroot
evidence.summary: The live process root is /srv/inventory-chroot. Chroot directories and worker executable are root-owned, and the host /etc/os-release is not visible from inside.

evidence.requirement: Make /var/lib/inventory the only writable application directory
evidence.summary: Namespace-level tests succeed writing to /var/lib/inventory and fail with read-only filesystem errors in /opt, /usr, and /var/lib. Probe artifacts were removed.
Post-reboot status shows the bash worker and sleep child active; its heartbeat advanced across a 35-second sample while remaining chrooted.

Healthy baseline boot ID 7223d5b7-fa56-4ff3-acee-959a5cf5f146 was captured, reboot acknowledged, new boot ID 1ce7546f-c544-4e34-96a0-44e70c6df861 observed, and service/data recovery directly verified.
